# OJAH — Organization for Justice & Accountability in the Horn of Africa

> OJAH is an African-led justice and accountability organization working across the Horn of Africa, with a current focus on Ethiopia. It monitors, investigates and documents human rights violations, preserves credible evidence, supports survivors and witnesses, and works with justice actors to confront impunity. Contact: communications@o-jah.org — 1612 K St NW, STE 400, Washington DC, USA.

## Pages

- [Home](https://o-jah.org/index.html): Overview of OJAH's mission, impact and featured publications
- [About](https://o-jah.org/about.html): Vision, mission, values and board leadership
- [What We Do](https://o-jah.org/what-we-do.html): Programme areas — documentation, justice actors, advocacy, survivor support, capacity building, memorialisation
- [How We Work](https://o-jah.org/how-we-work.html): Methodology and survivor-centred principles
- [Reports & Publications](https://o-jah.org/reports.html): Investigation and monitoring reports on Ethiopia, including "Stolen, Broken, Destroyed" (with Physicians for Human Rights), "Echoes of Violence", and "Broken Promises"
- [Stories & Updates](https://o-jah.org/stories.html): Survivor-centred accounts, told with consent and anonymized for safety
- [Contact](https://o-jah.org/contact.html): General, partnership, media and support enquiries
